newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnians to unite at Brussels aid conference.
newsitem.headline: Bosnians to unite at Brussels aid conference.

text.p: Bosnia's former warring sides will present joint plans for the country's reconstruction to foreign donors this week for the first time since the end of the war in 1995, international officials said on Tuesday.

Bosnia will be represented by officials from both the country's Moslem-Croat Federation, and the Serb Republic -- which boycotted the last such meeting -- at the donors' information conference in Brussels on Thursday and Friday.

"I think they (the Serbs) do accept that not attending the last conference was a mistake. We called it self-sanctions, they shot themselves in the foot with that and they seem to have recognised it," Colum Murphy, spokesman for the office of the High Representative in Bosnia, told Reuters.

International donors pledged $1.8 billion last year for reconstruction in 1996, of which the Serb Republic received a mere two percent because of its reluctance to accept the country's new joint institutions and its boycott of the pledging conference.
"I think they understood that there is a genuine catch-up programme of the international community. The fact that they received only two percent of aid is basically their own fault," Murphy said.

The World Bank and the European Union have recommended a $1.4 billion aid target for Bosnia's reconstruction in 1997 and the Bosnian government will offer a large number of projects to foreign donors, a World Bank official said.

Bosnia's main pledging conference for 1997 is set for March. Rory O'Sullivan, head of the World Bank's Sarajevo office, said 1996 showed an extraordinarily high rate of real handover of promised funds.
"Of the $1.8 billion pledged, the actual commitment was pretty well close to that -- $1.7 billion. It's never happened that commitments have equalled pledges in such a huge programme," he said.
The Bosnian inter-ethnic parliament appointed a peacetime cabinet on January 3, clearing the way for its rule over a loose union of the Serb and Moslem-Croat territories.
The country's Brussels delegation will consist of five members from each side and six members from the central government.
The delegation will be led by Foreign Trade and Economy Minister Hasan Muratovic.
"Housing is the first priority, to enable refugee returns. Second is employment and third is a social programme to enable a minimum social welfare," Muratovic told state television on Monday.
"Infrastructure reconstruction is the fourth objective and fifth is assisting Bosnia's budget, because revenues from customs and taxes will not cover necessary budget expenditures."
